description: Understands numbers, ways of representing them, relationships, and number sets.
Builds deductive and inductive logic to prove theorems related to numbers.
Discovers and proves algebraic identities; models real-life situations as equations.
Derives and uses formulae for areas, surface areas, and volumes.
Analyses properties of 2-D geometric shapes; develops mathematical arguments.
Analyses and interprets data using statistics and probability.
Perceives the axiomatic and deductive structure of Mathematics.
Builds visualisation, optimisation, representation, and modelling skills
Develops computational thinking; breaks complex problems into solvable sub-problems.
Appreciates contributions of Indian and global mathematicians.
Explores connections of Mathematics with other subjects.
Develops understanding of real numbers and their properties.
Understanding of powers (radical powers) and exponents.
States and proves remainder theorem, factor theorem, and division algorithm.
Models and solves contextualised problems using equations; draws conclusions.
Learns Brahmagupta's quadratic formula and uses it to solve problems.
Describes congruence of 2-D shapes to make and test conjectures.
Proves theorems using Euclid's axioms for triangles and quadrilaterals.
Proves theorems about circle GEOMETRY.
Understands the irrationality of pi and Madhava's infinite series.
Uses coordinate geometry to specify locations and solve problems.
Understands basic trigonometric functions, their history, and utility
Visualises and calculates areas using Heron's and Brahmagupta's formulae.
Calculates surface areas and volumes of cubes, cuboids, spheres, cylinders, and cones.
Applies measures of central tendency: mean, median, mode.
Applies probability concepts to solve problems on likelihood of everyday events..
Proves statements using stated assumptions, axioms, and definitions.
Visualises geometric proofs for algebraic identities.
Proves theorems using Euclid's axioms for angles, triangles, quadrilaterals, circles.
Constructs geometrical shapes satisfying given constraints.
Models daily-life phenomena using graphs, tables, and equations.
Uses 2-D representations of 3-D objects to solve surface area and volume problems.
Employs optimisation strategies to maximise quantities under given constraints.
Decomposes a problem into sub-problems
Describes and analyses a sequence of instructions.
Analyses similarities among problems to generalise one solution across multiple problems.
Engages in algorithmic problem-solving.
Recognises contributions of Indian and global mathematicians
Recognises modern contributions to Mathematics and next frontiers in the field.
Applies mathematical knowledge to problems in Science, Social Science, Arts, and Sports.
